$comment: Machine-readable MCP server profiles. Each server in opencode.json.mcp belongs to exactly one profile. Profiles are used by scripts/validate_mcp_profiles.py to enforce skill.requires_mcp coverage and by scripts/smoke_mcp_capabilities.py --mode to bound CI smoke probes. The descriptive trust matrix lives in docs/security/mcp-trust-boundaries.md and stays in sync via the validator.

base.description: Always-on lightweight servers. Low context cost, no required secrets, safe to spawn on every session. Skills in any domain may rely on these without justification.

research.description: Read-only documentation and source-search servers. Network calls only. No write surface. Higher context cost than `base` but bounded by skill design.

browser.description: Browser automation servers spawned via bunx. Required by skills in the Browser and Design domains for UI validation and debugging.

design.description: Design-system MCP surface (Figma frame context, shadcn registry). Skills in the Design domain depend on this profile.

repo.description: GitHub MCP for repository / PR / issue / actions surface. Listed separately because the GitHub MCP can pull very large context payloads (per OpenCode docs); skills must justify dependency.

high_context.description: Servers known to bring large context payloads — usually because they expose paginated GitHub / Drive / corp-tool data. Including these in a skill's `requires_mcp` is allowed only with a skill-specific justification.

ry-repair.github: Required for GitHub-aware repair flows that inspect remote issues, PRs, review context, and repository metadata. Local-only repair still uses local git/files first.
